summary: Code128 GTIN extraction relies solely on the text prefix '01' and does not enforce GS1 symbology or the exact 14-digit length required for AI (01). A plain Code128 or malformed GS1-128 can be misclassified as a valid GTIN.
claim: A non-GS1 Code128 barcode (e.g., internal custom code) encoding '01' + 14-digit number will be accepted as a GTIN, violating the requirement to accept Code128 only with GS1 AI (01). A GS1-128 with AI(01) followed by fewer than 14 digits may be padded and accepted, leading to false positives and incorrect data association.

evidence.source: In normalizeDecodedBarcode, the Code128 branch: val compact = text.replace("\u001d", "").removePrefix("]C1"); if (compact.startsWith("01")) Gtin.normalize(compact.drop(2).take(14))?.let { return it }. No check of result.resultMetadata for FNC1 or symbology identifier, and no length check after drop(2). The unit test nonGs1LinearFormatsCannotMasqueradeAsGtin only tests a 13-digit plain Code128 not starting with '01'; it does not test a plain Code128 containing '0107340002119380' or a malformed GS1-128 '019638936717461'.

suggested_remediation: In the Code128 branch, verify actual GS1 encoding (e.g., check result.resultMetadata for FNC1 or symbology identifier ']C1'), and after stripping '01' require exactly 14 digits before calling Gtin.normalize. Add unit tests rejecting plain Code128 '0107340002119380' and malformed '019638936717461'.
suggested_validation: A plain Code128 with text '0107340002119380' must return null. A true GS1-128 with FNC1 and the same text must return '07340002119380'. A Code128 with '019638936717461' must return null.
